title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: September 18, 2026 – Trades, Signings, and Season Previews Heat Up!

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Returns to Toronto in Blockbuster Deal!
items.summary: The Toronto Raptors have officially reacquired seven-time All-Star Kawhi Leonard from the LA Clippers in a long-delayed trade. The Raptors sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap, and two second-round picks to the Clippers to finalize the deal, ending a saga stemming from an NBA investigation into salary cap circumvention. Leonard, who led Toronto to the 2019 championship, will now pair with Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles, bolstering the Raptors' Eastern Conference contention hopes.

items.headline: Donovan Mitchell Inks Massive Extension with Cavaliers
items.summary: Cavs star Donovan Mitchell has finalized a four-year, maximum-salary extension, projected to be worth around $276 million, that will commence in the 2027-28 season. This significant deal solidifies Mitchell's long-term commitment to Cleveland, putting to rest earlier speculations about his potential departure.

items.headline: Stephen Curry Joins Li-Ning, Reiterates Warriors Loyalty
items.summary: Warriors superstar Stephen Curry has officially partnered with Chinese sportswear giant Li-Ning, signing a 10-year endorsement deal reportedly worth over $400 million, after parting ways with Under Armour in November 2025. Despite contract eligibility rumors, Curry affirmed his desire to remain a 'lifer' with Golden State, stating his mission to stay competitive with the team.

items.headline: Cavaliers Active in Offseason Trades, Draft
items.summary: Cleveland made significant moves, acquiring Peyton Watson via a sign-and-trade with the Nuggets, and Cam Whitmore from the Wizards in a five-team deal. They also traded the No. 29 pick (Alex Karaban) to the Kings for the No. 34 pick in the 2026 draft and a 2032 second-round pick.

items.headline: Kings Bolster Roster with Draft Talent
items.summary: Sacramento selected Darius Acuff Jr. as the No. 7 overall pick and Alex Karaban at No. 29 in the 2026 draft. They also signed second-rounder Emanuel Sharp to a guaranteed three-year deal, a rarity for a player drafted at No. 45.

items.headline: Devin Carter Waived by Hawks, Boston a Potential Suitor
items.summary: The Atlanta Hawks have waived guard Devin Carter, who averaged 8.9 points per game last season with Sacramento. With Atlanta still needing to trim its roster, Carter could find a new home, with Boston reportedly a possible destination.

items.headline: Derrick Jones Jr. Not Seeking Trade from Clippers
items.summary: Despite recent speculation, veteran forward Derrick Jones Jr. has not requested a trade from the LA Clippers. Sources indicate a strong relationship between Jones Jr. and the team, with both sides open to extension talks.

items.headline: James Harden Re-Signs with Cleveland
items.summary: James Harden has officially re-signed with the Cleveland Cavaliers on a three-year, $96.54 million contract. The deal includes a third-year player option and a 15% trade kicker, utilizing Non-Bird rights for the re-signing.

items.headline: Cavs Add Depth in Free Agency
items.summary: Beyond Mitchell's extension and Harden's re-signing, the Cavaliers secured Peyton Watson with a four-year, $88 million sign-and-trade deal. They also brought back Thomas Bryant on a one-year minimum and Mario Hezonja on a non-guaranteed minimum contract.

items.headline: Kings Make Key Free Agent Signings
items.summary: The Sacramento Kings made several notable free agency additions, re-signing Precious Achiuwa to a two-year, $11.2 million fully guaranteed deal and Daeqwon Plowden to a two-year minimum. They also signed Ben Simmons to a one-year, non-guaranteed minimum contract.

items.headline: Knicks Make Training Camp Additions
items.summary: The New York Knicks have made a series of training camp moves, signing Bruce Brown, James Wiseman, Ochai Agbaji, and Drew Eubanks to non-guaranteed Exhibit 9 contracts as they prepare for the upcoming season.

items.headline: Timberwolves Eyeing League Lead in Three-Pointers
items.summary: With the addition of LaMelo Ball, the Minnesota Timberwolves are projected to lead the NBA in three-point attempts this upcoming season. Anthony Edwards' continued improvement from deep is also expected to contribute to a more potent perimeter attack.

items.headline: Cap Space Driving Offseason Market Dynamics
items.summary: The 2026 NBA offseason is heavily influenced by cap space, creating a clear divide between financially flexible teams and those near the second apron. This disparity is shaping trade and free agency decisions, with cap-rich teams poised to accelerate market activity.

items.headline: EuroLeague Features Record Number of Former NBA Players
items.summary: The 2026-27 EuroLeague season will feature a record 133 former NBA players, collectively boasting over 20,000 regular-season games of experience. This marks an 11-player increase from last season, highlighting a growing connection between the two leagues.
